source_text: Potest et sic intellegi, fratres dilectissimi, ut quoniam mandat et monet Dominus etiam inimicos diligere et pro his quoque qui nos persecuntur orare, petamus et pro illis qui adhuc terra sunt et necdum caelestes esse coeperunt, ut et circa illos uoluntas Dei fiat quam Christus hominem conseruando et redintegrando perfecit. nam cum discipuli ab eo iam non terra appellentur sed sal terrae et apostolus primum hominem uocet de terrae limo, secundum uero de caelo, merito et nos qui esse debemus patri Deo similes, qui solem suum oriri facit super bonos et malos et pluit super iustos et iniustos, sic Christo monente oramus et petimus, ut precem pro omnium salute faciamus, ut quomodo in caelo id est in nobis per fidem nostram uoluntas Dei facta est ut essemus e caelo, ita et in terra hoc est in illis credere nolentibus fiat uoluntas Dei, ut qui adhuc sunt prima natiuitate terreni incipiant esse caelestes ex aqua et spiritu nati.
orientation: Cyprian is explaining the petition 'your will be done on earth as in heaven' by applying it to those not yet reborn from water and the Spirit.
pass_a_gloss: It can also be understood thus, most beloved brothers, that since the Lord commands and warns even to love enemies and to pray also for those who persecute us, we should ask also for those who are still earth and have not yet begun to be heavenly, that also concerning them God's will may be done, which Christ perfected by preserving and restoring man. For since the disciples are no longer called earth by him but salt of the earth, and the apostle calls the first man from the mud of the earth, but the second from heaven, deservedly also we who ought to be like God the Father, who makes his sun rise upon good and evil and rains upon just and unjust, thus with Christ warning we pray and ask, that we may make prayer for the salvation of all, that just as in heaven, that is in us through our faith, God's will has been done so that we might be from heaven, so also on earth, that is in those unwilling to believe, God's will may be done, that those who are still earthly by first birth may begin to be heavenly, born from water and the Spirit.

choices.why: Cyprian's standard address to his congregation; keeps the affectionate superlative and the fraternal address.
Keeps the stark biblical metaphor of being 'earth' before rebirth; 'still' preserves adhuc.
rejected: who are still of the earth

choices.why: Direct biblical phrase; the literal rendering is standard and recognizable.

choices.english: from the mud of the earth
choices.why: Limus is mud or slime, not just dust; keeps the material, earthy sense of the first man's origin.
rejected: from the dust of the earth

choices.why: Nolentibus is present participle of nolo, 'not wanting'; keeps the active refusal.

choices.english: born from water and the Spirit
choices.why: Echoes John 3:5; keeps the prepositional force of ex and the passive participle.
rejected: born again of water and the Spirit

bible_refs.note: diligere inimicos et pro his quoque qui nos persecuntur orare
primum hominem de terrae limo, secundum uero de caelo
solem suum oriri facit super bonos et malos et pluit super iustos et iniustos

pass_b_english: There is also another way to understand this, most beloved brothers. Since the Lord commands and warns us to love even our enemies and to pray for those who persecute us (Matthew 5:44), we should also pray for those who are still earth and have not yet begun to be heavenly. We ask that God's will be done in them as well—the will that Christ accomplished by preserving and restoring the human being. For when the disciples are no longer called earth by him but salt of the earth (Matthew 5:13), and the apostle calls the first man from the mud of the earth and the second from heaven (1 Corinthians 15:47), then rightly we too—who ought to be like God the Father, who makes his sun rise on the good and the evil and sends rain on the just and the unjust (Matthew 5:45)—pray and ask at Christ's instruction that we may make prayer for the salvation of all. Just as God's will has been done in heaven, that is, in us through our faith, so that we are from heaven, so may God's will also be done on earth, that is, in those unwilling to believe. so that those who are still earthly by their first birth may begin to be heavenly, born from water and the Spirit (John 3:5).

problems.why: Latin 'hominem' is singular 'man/human being', not collective 'humanity'; Christ accomplished this will in the individual human being he saved.
problems.fix: by preserving and restoring the human being

problems.quote: Those who are still earthly by their first birth may begin to be heavenly
problems.source_quote: ut qui adhuc sunt prima natiuitate terreni incipiant esse caelestes
problems.why: Latin 'ut... incipiant' expresses purpose ('so that they may begin'); English drops 'so that', making it a bare statement rather than the goal of the petition.
problems.fix: so that those who are still earthly by their first birth may begin to be heavenly
problems.ruling: 'ut...incipiant esse' is purpose clause completing the petition; dropping 'so that' misrepresents it as bare statement, not the prayer's goal.

edits.new: preserving and restoring the human being

edits.old: Those who are still earthly by their first birth may begin to be heavenly
edits.new: so that those who are still earthly by their first birth may begin to be heavenly

fixed: Changed 'humanity' to 'the human being' because the source has singular 'hominem', referring to the individual human being Christ saved.
Added 'so that' before 'those who are still earthly' because the source has 'ut... incipiant', expressing the purpose of the petition.

last_rejected.quote: and the apostle calls the first man from the mud of the earth and the second from heaven
last_rejected.source_quote: apostolus primum hominem uocet de terrae limo, secundum uero de caelo
last_rejected.why: Paul says the first man is 'of earth, made of dust' not 'from mud'; 'limo' likely 'limo' = 'of mud/dust' but Paul's point is origin, not composition.
last_rejected.fix: and the apostle calls the first man of the dust of the earth and the second of heaven
last_rejected.ruling: 'limo' means mud/slime/dust; 'from the mud of the earth' captures Paul's 'de terrae limo' accurately, origin and composition both implied.

last_rejected.quote: preserving and restoring the human being
last_rejected.why: Latin has present participles (conseruando et redintegrando), describing ongoing action, not a completed one ('accomplished').
last_rejected.ruling: Latin gerundives 'conseruando et redintegrando' denote means; 'accomplished' is acceptable for 'perfecit'.

last_rejected.quote: when the disciples are no longer called earth by him
last_rejected.source_quote: cum discipuli ab eo iam non terra appellentur
last_rejected.why: Subjunctive 'appellentur' with 'cum' indicates causal or concessive circumstance ('since/although'), not temporal 'when'.
last_rejected.fix: since the disciples are no longer called earth by him
last_rejected.ruling: 'cum' with subjunctive can be circumstantial/temporal; 'when' is a valid rendering here.

last_rejected.why: 'Merito' means 'rightly' in the sense of 'with good reason/justly', not temporal 'then'.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Then rightly' reads 'then' as connective, 'rightly' as 'merito'; acceptable English, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: pray and ask at Christ's instruction that we may make prayer for the salvation of all
last_rejected.source_quote: sic Christo monente oramus et petimus, ut precem pro omnium salute faciamus
last_rejected.why: 'Sic...ut' shows purpose/result: 'so...that we make prayer', not 'that we may make prayer' as a separate petition.
last_rejected.fix: so, at Christ's instruction, we pray and ask that we make prayer for the salvation of all
last_rejected.ruling: 'That we may make prayer' correctly renders purpose/result 'ut...faciamus'; 'may' is standard for subjunctive.

last_rejected.quote: so that we are from heaven
last_rejected.why: Subjunctive 'essemus' expresses purpose/result, not indicative fact; 'so that we might be from heaven' or 'so as to be heavenly'.
last_rejected.fix: so that we might be from heaven
last_rejected.ruling: 'So that we are from heaven' renders result clause 'ut essemus'; tense nuance is minor, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: so may God's will also be done on earth
last_rejected.source_quote: ita et in terra...fiat uoluntas Dei
last_rejected.why: Missing 'et' (also/too): should be 'so may God's will also be done on earth'—but more critically, 'ita...ut' correlation is weakened.
last_rejected.fix: so also on earth may God's will be done
last_rejected.ruling: English has 'also'; 'ita...ut' correlation is preserved; no major error.

last_rejected.why: Latin says 'in illis' (in them), referring to those still earthly; 'unwilling to believe' adds negative volition not in source ('nolentibus' goes with 'credere' as complementary infinitive: 'those not willing to believe').
last_rejected.fix: in those who refuse to believe
last_rejected.ruling: 'Nolentibus' + 'credere' means 'unwilling to believe'; English is accurate, not adding negative volition.

last_rejected.quote: so that those who are still earthly
last_rejected.source_quote: ut qui adhuc sunt prima natiuitate terreni
last_rejected.why: Missing 'prima natiuitate' (by their first birth): English has 'by their first birth' but source emphasizes this more prominently.
last_rejected.fix: so that those who by their first birth are still earthly
last_rejected.ruling: English includes 'by their first birth' for 'prima natiuitate'; no omission, no major error.
